key_insight: CORNETO’s ability to infer robust biological networks is not uniform across settings. Its reusability depends on the available data, prior biological knowledge, regularization and biological context.
problem_solved: Clarifies when a multi-omics network inference framework can be reused reliably, rather than assuming it will remain robust across datasets and biological settings.
method: Evaluate the reusability of CORNETO, an existing framework for learning biological networks from multi-omics data.
Examine how data availability, prior knowledge, regularization and biological context affect robustness.
Characterize distinct robustness regimes associated with prior knowledge and data availability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the findings emphasize that successful reuse requires checking data sufficiency and the suitability of prior knowledge. Robustness should be evaluated in the target biological setting, not assumed from earlier results.
visual_elements: Conceptual regime map with data availability and prior knowledge as axes, highlighting differing robustness conditions.
Pipeline diagram: multi-omics data and prior knowledge → CORNETO → inferred biological network.
Four-factor graphic showing data availability, prior knowledge, regularization and biological context.
Side-by-side network sketches illustrating stable versus variable inferred connections.
paper_title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
paper_authors: Xabier Martínez-de-Morentin, Sumeer A. Khan, Itziar Cenzano, Robert Lehmann, Alberto Maillo
